rv.q: Sensitively discussing themes of grief, family and community, this slow-burning drama satisfyingly blends humour, heart and melancholy.
Who is Kit Withington and please can she write all the new plays from now on?
The performances are rich and grounded.
Ultimately, Heart Wall bites off more than it can chew in well under two, interval-free hours.
Heart Wall is a beautifully structured, heartfelt piece that explores how death and life awkwardly co-exist in a way that feels fresh and true.
A triumph – warm, witty, and deeply human.

There is more than enough to it to keep the Bush Theatre audience entertained, but the play just doesn’t make the best use of its lengthy runtime, leading to a relatable if forgettable production that doesn’t leave much of a lasting impression.
It’s just a tad too sprawling and prosaic.
Perhaps with a few re-writes around the woollier plot-lines it could become a sharper and tighter vehicle, but there is already a great deal to enjoy.
Heart Wall is poignant and thought-provoking: with a tighter focus, it could deliver even more impact.
It all needs a stronger pulse and bloodflow to make for compelling drama.

cn.t: Critics praise Kit Withington's debut as a funny, poignant exploration of grief and belonging that blends humor with heart. The inventive karaoke-pub setting and strong performances earn acclaim for this thoughtful, character-driven family drama.
